pr.title: Sign off the release pull request's version bump in the Release workflow
pr.head: f00c7ec3407e35322ea7c80dac959e36df45ab63

summary: Projector ships a release through its Release workflow. Someone starts the workflow by hand, its propose job raises the version in pyproject.toml and the two plugin manifests on a release/vX.Y.Z branch, and opens a pull request. Merging that pull request tags and publishes the release.

main has a ruleset that requires the projector/review commit status, which a clean Projector review posts on the head it reviewed. No review session picks up a pull request that the workflow's own token opened, so every release pull request waited for a review that never came.

This change has the propose job sign off its own commit. The job first refuses a run dispatched from any ref but main. After the bump commit, it checks that the commit changes exactly the files in release.py's VERSION_FILES, and fails before the push when anything else changed. After the push, it posts a success projector/review status on that one commit. A later push to the release branch makes a new head with no status, which waits for a review like any other head.

The first review found that a run dispatched from another branch would carry that branch's commits into the release pull request under the status. The ref check fixes that, and the review of this head is clean.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Propose job: the Release workflow's job that runs on a manual dispatch and opens the release pull request.
  • projector/review: the commit status main's ruleset requires before a merge, normally posted by project review publish.
  • VERSION_FILES: the three files that carry Projector's version, listed in .github/scripts/release.py.
  • GITHUB_REF: the ref a run was dispatched from, such as refs/heads/main, which the runner sets.

cards.title: Review history so far
cards.html:
• 9ee2813: changes requested. A release dispatched from another branch would sign off that branch's unreviewed commits.
  • f00c7ec: clean. The job refuses any ref but main, and docs/plugins.md now describes the status.

groups.title: The propose job signs off its version bump
groups.kicker: A ref check, a guard on the release commit, then a success status on it
intro: The propose job gains statuses: write, the permission the commit statuses API needs. Its step now opens with a check that the run was dispatched from main, runs a guard between the commit and the force-push, and posts the status between the push and the pull request.

The ref check matters because actions/checkout takes the dispatched ref, and the release branch carries every commit that ref has. The guard lists the files the release commit changes, sorted, and compares them with the sorted VERSION_FILES that it imports from release.py. The status carries the description "Version-only release; needs no review" and links to the workflow run. The release pull request's body now says the workflow posted it.

files.note: The ref check, the guard, the status post, and the permission for it.

checks.text: The review ran these lines as the workflow writes them: refs/heads/main exits 0, and refs/heads/feature-x, refs/heads/main-x, and refs/tags/v0.8.18 exit 1 with run the release from main, not <ref>.
The only dispatch input is bump, so no input picks a ref. A re-run keeps the original run's GITHUB_REF and GITHUB_SHA, so it rebuilds from a commit that was on main at the dispatch.
The review replayed the job's commit and guard in a clone of the head. A plain patch bump passes and lists the three version files, and a bump with README.md also changed exits 1 and names it.
The active Projector review ruleset requires the projector/review context from any source, with no bypass, so a status posted with the workflow's token satisfies it.

files.note: The Release section now says the workflow posts the status, why a later push still needs a review, and that a run from another branch is refused.
"Release an update" now explains the status, the statuses: write permission, and the refusal of a run from another branch, beside its account of actions: write.
